item.title: Minato Mirai 21 Guide: Landmark Tower, Views & Access
item.description: Minato Mirai 21 (“Future Port”) is Yokohama’s glittering waterfront district and one of the Tokyo area’s best night-out destinations. Built on reclaimed harbour land, this sleek, futuristic quarter pairs the Landmark Tower — long Japan’s tallest building, with a 69th-floor Sky Garden observatory — with the giant Cosmo Clock 21 Ferris wheel, the historic Red Brick Warehouse, museums, malls and a romantic, illuminated bayfront promenade. Easy to reach and dazzling after dark, it’s the modern face of Yokohama and a perfect complement to the city’s Chinatown and old port heritage.

item.title: Yokohama Cosmo World Guide: Ferris Wheel, Rides & Access
item.description: In the heart of Yokohama’s Minato Mirai waterfront, Cosmo World is a compact, colourful amusement park crowned by one of the city’s most recognisable landmarks — the Cosmo Clock 21 Ferris wheel. Once the world’s tallest, this 112-metre giant clock-and-wheel glows in shifting colours after dark and offers a slow, romantic ride over the bay, the skyline and the illuminated harbour. Around it spin roller coasters, a splashy water ride and family attractions.

item.title: Yokohama Fireworks Guide: Summer Hanabi, Spots & Access
item.description: There are few sights more magical than fireworks (hanabi) bursting over Yokohama’s Minato Mirai skyline, their colours mirrored in the bay beside the glowing Ferris wheel and illuminated towers. Summer is firework season across Japan, and Yokohama’s waterfront — with its open harbour, parks and promenades — makes one of the country’s most photogenic backdrops. From large bay-side festivals to special event displays, tens of thousands gather on warm evenings in yukata to watch the sky light up.
